research_question: Among people who use tobacco, what is the effect of behavioural support on tobacco-use cessation compared with matched brief-advice or no-behavioural-support controls, while retaining three intervention-combination subgroups—behavioural support alone, behavioural support plus nicotine replacement therapy (NRT), and behavioural support plus varenicline—within one pooled analysis?
treatment_label: Behavioural support, classified as (1) behavioural support alone, (2) behavioural support + NRT, or (3) behavioural support + varenicline
control_label: Matched control: brief advice or no intervention for behavioural support alone; brief advice + NRT or NRT without intensive behavioural support for behavioural support + NRT; varenicline alone or varenicline without intensive behavioural support for behavioural support + varenicline
outcome_description: Tobacco-use cessation measured as abstinence from smoking or other tobacco use at the study-defined follow-up, including continuous/prolonged abstinence or point-prevalence abstinence verified biochemically or by self-report. Prefer the most rigorous available cessation definition within each study (continuous/prolonged over point prevalence; biochemically verified over self-report) and extract the longest reported follow-up unless a common review-defined follow-up is required. Pool all eligible cessation results as one target construct, with intervention-combination category entered as a prespecified subgroup.
positive_direction: A positive effect means that behavioural support, with or without matched pharmacotherapy, increases tobacco-use cessation relative to its matched control condition.
search_queries: behavioural support tobacco cessation controlled trial abstinence
smoking cessation counselling brief advice randomized trial
behavioural support nicotine replacement varenicline cessation trial
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies of people who use tobacco that evaluate behavioural support intended to promote tobacco-use cessation, either alone or combined with NRT or varenicline.

Studies containing a matched comparison condition consisting of brief advice, no intervention, NRT with absent or minimal behavioural support, or varenicline with absent or minimal behavioural support.
Studies reporting a quantitative tobacco-cessation or abstinence outcome from which an effect size can be calculated.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study; systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers are excluded.
No comparison between a behavioural-support treatment condition and an eligible matched control condition.
No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as event counts or proportions, means and standard deviations, t/F-values, or odds ratios.
Completely unrelated to behavioural support for tobacco-use cessation.
moderators_to_extract: Intervention-combination subgroup (behavioural support alone; behavioural support + NRT; behavioural support + varenicline)
Behavioural-support intensity and delivery mode (number/duration of contacts; individual, group, telephone, digital, or mixed)
Comparator type and intensity (no intervention, brief advice, or matched pharmacotherapy with minimal/no behavioural support)
Abstinence definition and biochemical verification status
Participant and tobacco-use characteristics, including tobacco product and population setting
effect_size_note: Conduct one pooled analysis with three prespecified intervention-combination subgroups: behavioural support alone versus brief advice/no intervention; behavioural support + NRT versus brief advice/minimal support + NRT; and behavioural support + varenicline versus varenicline alone/minimal support. Preserve each study arm as a separate comparison row. When multiple eligible behavioural-support variants share one control arm, include every eligible variant and divide the shared control group proportionally across comparisons (splitting both the control sample size and cessation-event count as closely as integer constraints permit) so participants are not double-counted; do not select or discard intervention variants. Keep matched pharmacotherapy balanced between intervention and control arms. Use a random-effects model with subgroup estimates and an overall pooled estimate, assess heterogeneity (tau-squared and I-squared), test subgroup differences, and conduct sensitivity analyses for abstinence definition, verification, follow-up duration, risk of bias, and alternative handling of correlated multi-arm comparisons where feasible.
